RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the August 1, 2006/Sravana 10, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions —20
Petroleum and Petrochemical
Investment Regions
*121. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
establishing Petroleum and Petrochemical
Investment Regions (PPCIR) in identified
ports, including Mangalore Port;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether certain major international
oil companies have evinced interest in the
proposed project;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the prospective investors
have aired some concerns over infrastructure
constraints, multiple clearances, tardy
litigation process and labour laws;
(f) if so, the details thereof and in what
manner Government propose to address
their concerns;
(g) whether like PPCIR, Manufacturing
Investment Regions are also proposed to
be established; and
(h) if so, the details thereof and the
locations identified for the purpose?
Permission for opening bank
branches in foreign countries
*122. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a few Public
Sector Banks have sought permission for
opening up of their branches in foreign
countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the decision so far taken
thereon and by when the remaining requests
are likely to be acceded to?

39
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
RBI Governor's meeting with Indian
Banks' Association
*123. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to refer to answer to
Unstarred Question 4014 given in the Rajya
Sabha on 23rd May, 2006 and state:
(a) whether any pre-credit policy meeting
was held between Governor, Reserve Bank
of India and Indian Banks' Association on
28th March, 2006; and
(b) what are the details of the
submissions made by the Chief Executive
of Indian Banks' Association in this meeting?
Budgetary support to PSUs for
payment of salaries
*124. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are giving
budgetary support to various loss making
Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to clear
the outstanding payment of salaries and
statutory dues to their employees;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the budgetary support
provided to each loss making PSU during
each of the last two years for industries
located in Andhra Pradesh?
Additional investment by ONGC
†*125. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that ONGC has
decided to make additional investment of
Rs. 4800 crore in order to increase
production of indigenous crude oil in the
year 2006-07;
(b) if so, the total annual amount of
additional investment made for increase in
production from April 2003-04 to March
2006-07;
(c) whether the increase in the
production post investment has also been
estimated; and
(d) if so, the quantity of likely additional
production during the current year?
Tax on interest paid to senior citizens
by banks
*126. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the interest
paid to senior citizens by banks and post
offices on investments made by them on
Senior Citizen Savings Scheme has been
made taxable income;
(b) if so, the reasons for bringing senior
citizens under tax net even under the above
Scheme which is meant exclusively for senior
citizens without any tax commitment; and
(c) what are the reasons for bringing
them under the tax net now when the
scheme was introduced in 2004 and banks
and post offices have so far not been
deducting any tax on investments so made
during the last two years by senior citizens?
Profit on petrol and diesel
*127. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the margin of profit of private and

40
public sector oil-companies per litre of
petrol and diesel; and
(b) the total amount of tax, duties,
excise etc. on petrol and diesel per litre?
New airport in Assam for
Asian Safari
*128. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMYUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the a private
Thai airline operator has proposed making
the State part of an Asian Safari circuit and
is interested in building an airport in Assam;
(b) whether the Bangkok Airways is
interested in building an airport near the
Kaziranga National Park and other facilities
to make Assam an Asian Safari Destination;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Inadequate supply of gas to two gas
turbines at Ramgarh Gas

RAJYA  SABHA

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the August 1, 2006/Sravana 10, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 154
164
Growth opportunities in aviation
sector
710. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
introduced number of measures and steps
i.e. modernisation of airports, new aircrafts
ordered, ATF excise duty halved, travel
tax abolished and landing charges reduced
etc.;
(b) if so, whether some more initiatives
are yet to be taken for growth
opportunities in aviation sector;
(c) whether Government have
demonstrated its commitment by
launching the airport modernisation
programme to ensure speedy
implementation (both at major hubs and
35 small airports) to match with the traffic
growth; and
(d) if so, what are the main steps
considered and to what extent it has been
successful?
Expansion of civil aviation industry
711. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether India at the Annual General
Meeting of the International Air Transport
Association (IATA) held at Paris this year,
indicated an elaborate plan for expansion
of Civil Aviation industry both in the public
and private sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
plans for expansion of industry in the
domestic and international sector to
unshackle it from the restrictive policies of
the past; and
(c) the steps taken and being taken in
pursuance thereof?
Security clearance for airlines
712. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the details pertaining to the
requirement for private commercial airlines
to obtain ‘security clearance’ from
Government;

165
(b) the details of security clearances
issued to airlines operating commercial
flights in India showing the date of
commencement of commercial flight
operation by each;
(c) whether security clearance pertaining
to the Promoters and Directors of M/s Jet
Air had been pending to be issued;
(d) if so, details thereof, indicating the
reasons for its remaining pending;
(e) the basis of permitting the said
Airlines to operate despite non-issuance
of security clearance;
(f) whether the same have since been
issued; and
(g) if so, details thereof?
New airline service in Kerala
713. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Kerala supported project of starting a new
airline by Cochin International Airport Ltd.
(CIAL) has been presented to the Central
Government;
(b) if so, what are the reasons for which
the Central Government are delaying
sanction to this project; and
(c) what steps would be taken to
expedite the same?
Infrastructure bottlenecks faced by
airports
714. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are working
on developing not only the airports in
the metro cities but also in at least 35
non-metro cities using public-private
partnership at Rs. 7000-8000 crore;
(b) whether Government are considering
checking the infrastructure bottlenecks
being faced at airports around the country;
(c) whether Planning Commission is
considering relaxation of environmental
clearance norms for these airports including
complete exemption from environmental
clearance for development, construction
and expansion;
(d) if so, to what extent this will help in
completing the projects; and
(e) whether Airports Authority of India
has started developing these airports?
Technical check-up of aircrafts
715. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of flights operating
in the country which are owned by various
companies, company-wise;
(b) whether the DGCA has any
permanent arrangement for the regular
technical check-ups for over all conditions
of the flights; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Complaints against private airlines
716. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any complaints regarding functioning of
private airlines, especially customer service;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken against those airlines
providing inadequate services?

166
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Increase in flying age of pilots

the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be

(a) whether Government have recently
increased flying age of pilots from 60 to 65
years subject to certain conditions;
(b) if so, the details of conditions subject
to which Government would enhance flying
age of pilots;
